explanations.q1: Both variables reference the same list object, so appending to one updates the shared list.
explanations.q2: Default arguments are evaluated once at function definition time. The list keeps previous state across calls, so the second call becomes [1, 1].
explanations.q3: Slicing with [::-2] starts from the end and steps by -2, so the result is [4, 2].
explanations.q4: The inner loop runs for i, i+1, ..., n-1, giving a triangular count of O(n^2).
explanations.q5: Insertion sort performs very well on nearly sorted arrays because it makes few swaps/moves.
explanations.q6: In a BST, all nodes in the left subtree are smaller than the root node.
explanations.q7: The expression is evaluated as (a++) + (++a), so it becomes 5 + 7 = 12.
explanations.q8: Runtime polymorphism is achieved through virtual methods and overriding.
explanations.q9: The protected access specifier allows access within the class and derived classes.
explanations.q10: A pure virtual function requires derived classes to override it before objects can be instantiated.
explanations.q11: Deadlock requires mutual exclusion, hold and wait, circular wait, and no preemption.
explanations.q12: Round Robin allocates a time quantum and cycles through processes in order.
explanations.q13: LEFT JOIN returns all rows from the left table and matched rows from the right side, with NULLs otherwise.
explanations.q14: IP is the network-layer protocol responsible for packet forwarding between networks.
explanations.q15: The midpoint formula low + (high - low) / 2 prevents overflow in large integer ranges.
explanations.q16: In a min-heap, the root always contains the minimum value.
explanations.q17: The ternary conditional chooses the larger value, which is 20.
explanations.q18: Compilation is not a core OOP principle; encapsulation, inheritance, and polymorphism are.
explanations.q19: Big-O describes the upper bound on growth as input size increases, typically the worst-case trend.
explanations.q20: An abstract class may contain pure virtual functions and cannot be instantiated directly.
